back: Data together with the operations on it, defined without saying how it is stored.
Last in, first out. Push and pop at the top; a stack pointer marks the top item; peek reads it without removing.
First in, first out. Enqueue at the rear, dequeue at the front; front and rear pointers.
The rear pointer wraps to place 1 after the last place (Rear ← MOD(Rear, Size) + 1) so freed places are reused; a count shows full or empty.
Nodes of data and pointers; a start pointer marks the first node and a null pointer ends the list.
The unused nodes linked together; a new item takes the first free node and a deleted node is returned to the free list.
Take a free node, store the item, set its pointer to the next node and make the previous node point to it.
Make the previous node point to the node after the deleted one and add the deleted node to the free list.
Stack for undo or back; queue for print jobs or waiting customers; linked list for a sorted list with many insertions and deletions.
